target_customer: Process chemists and innovation heads at pharma and biotech companies, and lab equipment makers
problem: Chemical process development relies on trial and error or exhaustive screening, delaying drug manufacturing scale-up.
business_model: B2B software platform and API plus consulting, HTE plates and data services
product_category: AI and Bayesian optimization for chemical process development

founders.name: Alexander Pomberger
education: PhD, Machine Learning for Chemistry, University of Cambridge
founders.background_notes: YC page says PhD in chemical engineering; launch post says Cambridge.

founders.name: Daniel Wigh
education: PhD, Machine Learning for Chemistry, University of Cambridge

investors: unnamed venture capitalists and angels (about 1.5M USD)

technical_complexity.rationale: Transfer learning and Bayesian optimization validated in the wet lab, plus integration with robotic reactors, need PhD-level ML and chemistry skills.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms and proprietary descriptors are specialized and pharma pilots create switching costs, but academic methods are published and Atinary and others compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in March 2025 names legacy statistical software like JMP and unnamed startups as alternatives; no incumbent copied or bought it in sources found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reports 12 pilot trials with pharma companies, some Big Pharma; the company says process design delays FDA trials for months and claims up to 95 percent fewer experiments.

branding.domain_note: Uses reactwise.com; YC page also lists react-wise.com.

identity.visual_style: scientific software, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 badges
identity.voice_and_tone: scientific and practical (AI Co-Pilot for Chemical Process Optimization)

branding.brand_signature: Ask Vera copilot and MemoryBO product names
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch coverage on 2025-03-17 and biopharma trade press; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name combines react (chemistry) and wise (smart), but this reading is my inference and not stated by sources; TechCrunch and trade coverage helped awareness.

outcome_analysis: ReactWise, founded by two Cambridge PhDs in machine learning for chemistry, raised a 3.4 million dollar pre-seed in March 2025 including YC money and an Innovate UK grant, ran pilots with pharma customers and now lists Pfizer and Pharmaron in testimonials. No later round or exit was found, so it is an active early company with credible domain fit.
notes: Round confirmed by TechCrunch and BioPharmaTrend; one aggregator shows 1.6M as a grant, which matches the Innovate UK component. Competitor search returned research papers and later vendor pages, nothing dated near mid 2024, so list is empty; Atinary (SDLabs) and Sunthetics are adjacent players per later sources. Founder prior employers not listed on YC page; Pomberger's Big Pharma history comes from TechCrunch. Location Cambridge UK per YC; some profiles say San Francisco or London.
